title: Persisted manifest unit_ref can escape its normalized-instance directory
summary: A lower-trust adopted KCS store can persist an absolute or parent-traversing `unit_ref`. Both normalized-unit readers append `.json`, join the unvalidated value to the instance directory, and read the result with the victim user's filesystem authority. A compatible external normalized unit can then enter current-scope chunks, indexing, or incremental previous context.

severity.rationale: Cross-scope normalized text and evidence provenance can be exposed or contaminated, giving High impact. Likelihood is Medium because exploitation requires adoption of lower-trust persisted state, a predictable victim-readable JSON target, a schema-compatible normalized unit, a later eligible invocation, and for reliable live search, compatible provenance fields. The immutable attack-path decision is Medium/P2.
severity.changeConditions: Severity would increase if untrusted store import were automatic or victim normalized-unit paths were broadly predictable with direct attacker readback. It would decrease if imported stores were always fully revalidated and unit references were derived and opened only beneath a trusted instance directory.

confidence.rationale: The exact revision provides a complete manifest-to-read-to-index/reuse trace. A bounded offline regression exercised absolute and parent-component references with synthetic unit JSON and observed the external marker in the vulnerable model while the derived-reference fixed model rejected both. No production-store or shared-service readback was executed.

taxonomy.category: Path traversal and cross-scope normalized-data import

codeEvidence.label: Persisted manifest accepts unit_ref as an unconstrained string
codeEvidence.code:
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct NormalizedUnitManifestEntry {
    pub order: u64,
    pub unit_key: String,
    pub unit_ref: String,
    pub unit_type: UnitType,
    pub status: UnitStatus,
    pub prepared_hash: String,
    pub error_kind: Option<String>,
}
codeEvidence.explanation: An adopted store contributor controls the deserialized `unit_ref`. The type does not distinguish a derived local identifier from an absolute or parent-bearing path string, so the value reaches both readers without a format or containment guarantee.

codeEvidence.label: Normal writers derive a 16-hex local object identifier
codeEvidence.explanation: The writer-side invariant is that the filename stem is derived from `unit_key`, yielding only 16 lowercase hexadecimal characters. The vulnerable readers do not reapply this derivation before reading persisted state.

codeEvidence.label: Rebuild reader joins and reads the manifest-controlled reference
codeEvidence.explanation: For every `Done` entry, KCS appends `.json`, joins the contributor-controlled string to `dir`, and immediately calls `fs::read()`. An absolute component replaces `dir`; parent components traverse it. Successful parsing carries the external object's markdown and provenance into `NormalizedUnitInput`.

codeEvidence.label: Externally selected markdown is chunked under the current tree entry
codeEvidence.explanation: The units returned by the uncontained read are paired with the current tree entry's `raw_path` and chunked for derived index state. This is where external normalized content can acquire current-scope attribution.

codeEvidence.label: Previous-instance loading repeats the uncontained read
codeEvidence.explanation: The incremental path performs the same join and read. A parseable external object is accepted into `units`, which can become previous normalized context for a later adapter operation.

rootCause.summary: KCS persists `unit_ref` as if it were a derived local object identifier but deserializes it as an unrestricted string. Normal writers derive a safe 16-hex value from `unit_key`; the rebuild and previous-instance readers do not re-derive or validate that value, do not reject separators or absolute paths, and do not prove direct-child containment before `fs::read()`. The resulting external unit is then consumed as current-scope chunking input or incremental previous context.

remediation: Treat `unit_ref` as a derived identifier, not a path. In every reader, compute `kcs_pipeline::prepare::unit_ref(entry.unit_key)`, reject any persisted value that differs, and construct the filename only from the computed value. Centralize the logic for rebuild and previous-instance loading, validate the unit object's provenance tuple before consumption, and use direct-child/no-follow opening or equivalent containment defense in depth.

validation.method: Exact-revision static source trace plus bounded offline synthetic path regression
validation.summary: Static review traced contributor-controlled persisted metadata through both path joins and reads to index chunking and incremental reuse. The bundled temporary-directory regression loaded a synthetic external marker for both an absolute reference and a parent traversal in the vulnerable model; the fixed derived-reference model rejected both and accepted a canonical in-instance control.
assertions: An absolute formatted unit filename replaces the intended instance base.
A parent-bearing unit reference selects a JSON object outside the instance directory.
Both production readers lack a canonical-reference or containment check before `fs::read()`.
The synthetic fixed model rejects both malicious references and accepts the canonical control.
limitations: The regression is source-faithful but does not invoke the KCS CLI end to end.
No real `.kcs` store, non-synthetic file, credential, external service, or shared-store readback was used.
Victim path predictability and the prevalence of adopted lower-trust stores were not measured.

attackPath.summary: A lower-trust contributor supplies an adopted store with a `Done` manifest entry whose `unit_ref` is absolute or parent-traversing. A later victim rebuild or incremental workflow reads a compatible normalized-unit JSON outside the instance with victim authority, then chunks or reuses its markdown under the current scope.

dataflow.summary: adopted `manifest.json` unit_ref -> `.json` suffix and unchecked path join -> victim-authority `fs::read()` -> `NormalizedUnitObject` parse -> current-scope chunking/index or previous context
dataflow.source: contributor-controlled `unit_ref` in a lower-trust adopted normalized manifest
dataflow.outcome: cross-scope normalized text import and derived-state/evidence contamination

reachability.summary: Reachability is local and filesystem-mediated. The victim must adopt supplied persisted state, the contributor must know or arrange a readable compatible JSON target, and the victim must run rebuild/index or incremental processing.
reachability.entrypoint: a persisted normalized manifest in an adopted `.kcs` store
reachability.outcome: an external normalized unit is consumed under the adopted scope

impact.why: A selected unit can contain sensitive normalized text from another scope, and its markdown can contaminate chunks, index attribution, evidence, or incremental context.

likelihood.why: The path requires lower-trust store adoption, victim-readable target knowledge, schema compatibility, later operator invocation, and potentially compatible provenance fields for reliable live search.

limitations: The primitive appends `.json` and cannot directly disclose arbitrary non-JSON files.
Operating system permissions bound the readable targets.
Direct disclosure back to the contributor requires a later readback channel.

remediationTests: Reject absolute `unit_ref` values before any unit read in both normalized-unit readers.
Reject `../`, embedded separators, uppercase, overlong, and otherwise non-canonical references.
Reject a valid-looking 16-hex reference that does not equal the value derived from the entry's `unit_key`.
Reject symlinked or canonically escaped unit objects without a time-of-check/time-of-use gap.
Accept a canonical in-instance unit and verify all object provenance fields against the manifest and requested tuple.
Run an end-to-end rebuild and incremental regression that asserts an external marker never reaches chunks, search/evidence state, or previous adapter context.
preventiveControls: Centralize all persisted normalized-instance reads behind one validated loader.
Represent derived object references with a validated newtype instead of `String`.
Open store objects relative to trusted directory handles with no-follow semantics where supported.
Fully validate imported stores before they are eligible for rebuild, search, or incremental reuse.
